title: Michel de Seure (Lisbon) to de Fresne and Henri II, December 1558: BnF fr. 3151 nos. 39-41, 43-44

steps.what: Located the Seure letters in fr. 3151: six, not the one the catalogue lists (nos. 39-44; 40/41 and 43/44 duplicates).
Seure letters (nos. 39-44): ~2,000 signs, homophonic plus nomenclator, no decipherment; left open as too large for this pass.

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): catalogue item 10 had grouped three letters in three different ciphers. La Guiche's 22-sign substitution stays in guiche1551; Noailles's Venice letter (another symbol alphabet) went to noailles1558 and Seure's six Lisbon letters (homophonic with numeral codes) to seure1558.

Angus Robinson (PR #40) used the three deciphered paragraphs A, B, C on a leaf inserted in the volume, which overlap the cipher of no. 44, as cribs; he then found that no. 43's postscript enciphers the same text as no. 44 C and that no. 40 has clear copies of its enciphered parts.

Contributor: best-effort transcription of all five letters (9,405 positions, 397 rows), then simulated annealing from the cribs (four parallel runs); look-alike signs first merged were split by repeated comparison with the scans, reducing about 230 proposed characters to 118 sign types; a held-out section deciphered with the final key.

Checked here: the decipherment of each letter scores as French (lang.lm best_language: fr-1600-letters first for nos. 39, 40, 41, 43, 44, -1.99 to -2.13 per letter); sections 41a/c/d, 44A/B/C and 43mid/43ps measured as the same text in three witnesses; rows 1-9 of no. 39 compared with Gallica view 72 sign by sign.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 9367 tokens, 121 types, fr-1530-despatches order 4: reading -2.269 per letter; random keys -5.406 (z 13.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.653 (mean -3.697, z 56.0); annealer on the real text -2.634. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.231; polyphony 0.007; 38 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.634

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Angus Robinson (PR #40) recovered the key from cribs supplied by three short deciphered paragraphs bound beside no. 44, then annealing and manual correction against the scans; the project checked it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: KEY_AND_DECRYPTION.txt (PR #40): 8,819 of 8,857 signifying positions (9,405 positions less 499 nulls and 49 cancellation signs) carry a key value; 28 unread ([...]) and 10 contextual readings counted as unread.

gaps.detail: unassigned word sign; contributor proposes vostre from context

gaps.detail: left [...] by the contributor; a further 10 read only from context

outcome.notes: Contributed. longs_x = escuz is conjectural (one occurrence). Contributor estimates at least 18 scribal errors in 9,405 positions.

credits.note: PR #40: key (118 signs, 21 nulls, cancellation sign) and full decipherment of nos. 39-41, 43-44, from cribs on the adjacent deciphered leaf plus annealing and manual correction

prior.where: A leaf in fr. 3151 carries three short deciphered paragraphs (A, B, C) of no. 44's cipher; no full decipherment in print or online found by the contributor or here.

human: Project-level: the target was catalogued and split here (item 10). 16 Oct 2026: outside contributor Angus Robinson (GitHub AngusRobinson, PR #40) sent the key and full decipherment, working with an AI collaborator he calls Sol; the project checked it (LM language check, statistical validation, spot-check of no. 39 against view 72).
